definitions.explanation: A fish of the northern Pacific, caught mainly off Hokkaido. Best known split open, salted, dried, and grilled as ホッケの{開|ひら}き, a staple of izakaya menus.

examples.japanese: ホッケ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}いた→焼く：01123_yaku⟧。
⟦{居酒屋|いざかや}→居酒屋：09635_izakaya⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ホッケ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{開|ひら}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{頼|たの}んだ→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧。
examples.english: At the izakaya I ordered a grilled split Atka mackerel.

examples.japanese: ⟦{北海道|ほっかいどう}→北海道：11010_hokkaidou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ホッケ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大|おお}きくて→大きい：00335_ookii⟧⟦{脂|あぶら}→脂：01916_abura⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧のって⟦いて→いる：00495_iru⟧、⟦{大根|だいこん}おろし→大根おろし：26890_daikonoroshi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{合|あ}う→合う：10466_au⟧。
examples.english: Hokkaido Atka mackerel are big and fatty, and go well with grated daikon.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ホッケ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{開|ひら}き: Atka mackerel split, dried, and grilled
- ⟦{焼|や}き→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ホッケ / ホッケ{焼|や}き: grilled Atka mackerel
- ⟦{縞|しま}→縞：27905_shima⟧ホッケ: a striped related species, often imported

CULTURAL NOTE:
A large grilled ホッケ, shared with grated daikon and soy sauce, is a classic izakaya dish. It is mostly eaten as a ⟦{干物|ひもの}→干物：12423_himono⟧ (dried fish) rather than fresh.

WRITING:
The kanji is rare, so the word is written in katakana.
